title: Efficient Realization of Quantum Encryption
summary: Every known scheme has the required efficient realization, but whether this follows for every efficiently implementable encryption algorithm remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Determine whether there exists a quantum encryption scheme whose encryption algorithm $\operatorname{Enc}_k$ is efficiently implementable, but for which the following realization is not efficiently implementable: sample a random pure auxiliary state from a probability distribution, attach it to the plaintext, and apply a unitary operator. Each of these three steps is efficiently implementable for every known scheme, but it is unresolved whether this must hold for every scheme with an efficiently implementable $\operatorname{Enc}_k$.

scope.domain: Quantum encryption schemes and efficient implementation of their encryption algorithms.
parameters: The key k, which indexes the encryption algorithm
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether there exists a quantum encryption scheme with an efficiently implementable encryption algorithm but a specified realization, consisting of auxiliary-state sampling, attachment to the plaintext, and unitary application, that is not efficiently implementable.

progress.summary: The source states that the three-step realization is efficiently implementable for every scheme known to the authors, then explicitly leaves open whether every efficiently implementable encryption algorithm has such a realization.
citation_labels: Gorjan Alagic et al., Unforgeable Quantum Encryption
